final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Metric-surface case ('Service quality degradation.'): object layer is clean exclusion evidence — all train-ticket pods 2/2 Running, RESTARTS 0, nodes Ready, no FailedScheduling/FailedCreate/FailedMount/OOM events (only rollout probe noise), and the alerted pods span worker-01/02/03 (no node-scope fault). Alerts (12:52:59~12:54:54) show CPU saturation across the order/payment path (ts-order-service, ts-inside-payment-service, ts-payment-service, ts-security-service, ts-user-service) with a traffic surge on ts-security-service. Only ts-order-service carries a real limit-hit deviation: 'RESOURCE_SATURATION [cpu_cfs] | Val: 0.732s (Throttled)' against its configured cpu limit of 500m (requests 200m); the peers sit at 0.02-0.06 cores, far below their caps, and their +74%/+197% rows ride near-zero baselines and carry no throttle of their own (ripple/collateral). The call graph closes on it: ts-security-service and ts-inside-payment-service directly call ts-order-service (ts-inside-payment also calls ts-payment-service), so the alerted set is its immediate call neighbourhood; caller-side evidence follows at ts-inside-payment-service, which logs inside the window 'Payment failed: Pay Failed, order not found with order id 4682bf2d-...' (12:53:36) and '...f5f510a5-...' (12:54:22) plus repeated pay/drawBack retries ('Order status Not allowed to Pay'), while ts-order-service's own log stream stays INFO-only (no error rows). Diagnosis: the ts-order-service pod's CPU load exceeds its 500m limit and is CFS-throttled, degrading service quality and rippling CPU/traffic saturation to its callers. (Note: the just-updated workspace constraint list names boutique apps, but namespace boutique holds no resources in this snapshot — the active diagnosed environment and tool enums are train-ticket, so the train-ticket unit is used.)

This wording lives on the metric surface — the alerts name the case, and the object layer is only the exclusion. Read the alerts first, and the case you land on decides:

1. **Alerts first.** `GetAlerts` tells you whose anomaly it is, which kind (latency / saturation / throughput / traffic), and at what scope. Unlike the reachability wordings, opening from the object layer here is not troubleshooting — the signal is in the metrics. When several alerts fire at once the case is the **primary anomaly** — the service the other alerts ripple from, carrying the runaway deviation: read the rows' shape before their size — a latency row that moves only its p90 is a partial-traffic ripple (only the traffic sharing a path with the degraded pod slowed), while the row whose p50 and p90 both move carries the delay across all of its traffic and marks the epicenter; among those both-percentile rows the epicenter carries the steepest p90 escalation, and the graph closes it (`GetServiceDependencies`): every ripple is its direct neighbor, so a candidate that would need a quiet intermediate hop is not the source. Percentages on near-zero baselines prove nothing. A saturation row counts only when it rides on that epicenter **and comes with the service's own latency rise** — a genuine resource fault shows the throttle *and* its own latency climbing together; a bare `cpu_cfs` row on a service that is not the epicenter, with no latency of its own, is collateral noise — don't out-rank the runaway deviation with it. A `LATENCY_MISSING` row ("metrics dropped to zero/NaN") is a hole the collection left in the injection window, not a service's deviation — it never names the case, so don't anchor on it. And when a whole-system network-drop sweep carries no latency row at all, the epicenter is the point every request flows through (the system's total traffic) — its collapse is the source, the rest is the ripple. Apply the branches below to the primary anomaly, not to the loudest keyword.
2. **Deal with the case you land on:**
   - **Saturation rows on one service** (`RESOURCE_SATURATION [cpu_cfs]` / `[cpu core]` / memory) → it's a resource fault on that service's pods: read its pods face (usage vs limits) to close.
   - **A constant delay riding on one service's own latency** — its p50/p90 jump by a fixed amount, its callers see the same added delay, its downstream server-side latencies stay clean, no saturation rows → `pod_network_delay`: the delay sits on that pod's network path. Don't reach for a code explanation — an artificial delay *in code* is a code-defect (a different wording, and it has to be shown from the code surface); under this wording a delay case is network-side.
   - **The same latency / packet anomaly across every pod on one node** (scope it with the pods listing's NODE column) → it's a node-scope network fault: read the node objects (conditions / node runtime services) to close.
3. **Close by excluding the object layer.** The pods / deployments / services / endpoints / nodes listings show everything else healthy — RESTARTS 0, AVAILABLE 1/1, endpoints bound, nodes Ready, no mechanism events. apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-order-service
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ts-order-service
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ts-order-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ts-order-service
        image: ghcr.io/sregym/ts-order-service:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        env:
        - name: SPRING_MAIN_ALLOW_CIRCULAR_REFERENCES
          value: 'true'
        - name: NODE_IP
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.hostIP
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: ts-order-mysql
        - configMapRef:
            name: nacos
        - configMapRef:
            name: rabbitmq
        ports:
        - containerPort: 12031
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 350Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
        readinessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 12031
          initialDelaySeconds: 60
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-order-service
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 12031
  selector:
    app: ts-order-service
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-order-mysql
type: Opaque
stringData:
  ORDER_MYSQL_HOST: tsdb-mysql-leader
  ORDER_MYSQL_PORT: '3306'
  ORDER_MYSQL_DATABASE: ts
  ORDER_MYSQL_USER: ts
  ORDER_MYSQL_PASSWORD: Ts_123456

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-inside-payment-service
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ts-inside-payment-service
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ts-inside-payment-service
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ts-inside-payment-service
        image: ghcr.io/sregym/ts-inside-payment-service:latest
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        env:
        - name: SPRING_MAIN_ALLOW_CIRCULAR_REFERENCES
          value: 'true'
        - name: NODE_IP
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.hostIP
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: ts-inside-payment-mysql
        - configMapRef:
            name: nacos
        ports:
        - containerPort: 18673
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 200m
            memory: 350Mi
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 512Mi
        readinessProbe:
          tcpSocket:
            port: 18673
          initialDelaySeconds: 60
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-inside-payment-service
spec:
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 18673
  selector:
    app: ts-inside-payment-service
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  namespace: train-ticket
  name: ts-inside-payment-mysql
type: Opaque
stringData:
  INSIDE_PAYMENT_MYSQL_HOST: tsdb-mysql-leader
  INSIDE_PAYMENT_MYSQL_PORT: '3306'
  INSIDE_PAYMENT_MYSQL_DATABASE: ts
  INSIDE_PAYMENT_MYSQL_USER: ts
  INSIDE_PAYMENT_MYSQL_PASSWORD: Ts_123456
